clue.text: Extremely good man entering in church

indicators.note: entering tells us the good man goes into the word for extremely

parts.note: extremely means very
ST, short for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A notably virtuous man walks into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts ST (saint) inside VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy-style room inside a place of worship where clergy robe is this.

parts.note: reads like a turn in a game, but 'go' here means energy and liveliness

explanation.walkthrough: 'go' as a noun means pep or energy, not a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Go in the sense of energy and liveliness is a synonym.

clue.text: Equestrian ability acquired by large majority

definitions.meaning: a rider's secure position in the saddle
a constituency where a party's majority is so big it cannot lose

explanation.surface: A rider's skill was gained by a big margin.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a constituency held by a large majority is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm hold in the saddle for a rider, and an electoral constituency one party is certain to keep.

clue.text: Tumbledown place I am brought in to manage

indicators.note: brought in says the letter for the speaker is placed inside the verb for manage

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newcomer is hired to run a dilapidated property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts I inside RUN; 'am' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecked, collapsed building is a description of this.

clue.text: A foundation garment is put back on showing wear

parts.note: a bra is a foundation garment, women's underwear

indicators.note: put back tells us the little word is is turned round

parts.note: taken as written before reversal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worn-out bra is put on again, showing signs of wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear in the sense of scraping and erosion of a surface is a synonym.

parts.note: sounds like a best-selling author, but means the commonest writing implement

explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is the instrument used to write, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The biro is the most widely used pen, a thing that writes.

definitions.meaning: a curved opening one passes under, as in a gateway
the curved part of the sole of the foot

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: a curved passage and the raised part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved gateway structure, and the curved underside of the foot between heel and ball.

parts.note: sounds like a forceful person, but means a typeface used for emphasis

explanation.walkthrough: 'type' is printing type, not a kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanted print is the usual typographic way of stressing a word.

clue.text: Sewer one has to thread one's way through

definitions.text: Sewer one has to thread one's way through

parts.words: Sewer one has to thread one's way through
parts.note: sounds like a drain to be navigated, but a sewer here is one who sews, using a tool with an eye to thread

explanation.surface: Picking a path through a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' is someone who sews, not a drain; you literally thread the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing implement with an eye for thread is what a sewer uses.

clue.text: Light meal for a pet at home

parts.note: a pet is a sulk or fit of temper, as is a tiff
at home is in

explanation.surface: A snack for the household animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' means a fit of pique, as in 'in a pet'; TIFFIN is an Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Indian term for a light midday snack or lunch.

parts.note: sounds like money placed in the City of London, but invest also means besiege

explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' in military terms means to surround a town; the City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Investing a town in the military sense means sealing it off by siege.

parts.note: a journey out and back, read literally as a ring-shaped excursion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' is taken literally: a loop journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey that loops back to its start is literally round.

indicators.note: may be suggests the word lots could be turned into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Plenty of things could have gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing items cannot be found, a straight synonym.

definitions.meaning: Jack Frost personifies frosty weather, which is chilly

explanation.surface: Agile as the spirit of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Frost is the folk personification of frost.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both quick on one's feet and biting cold, as frosty weather is.

definitions.meaning: an invoice or statement of charges
a hooked blade used to cut and prune branches

explanation.surface: An invoice for hedge-trimming work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a billhook, a gardener's hooked blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice, and a hooked gardening blade also known as a billhook.

parts.note: ff is the musical marking for fortissimo, very loud
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Taking part in a very loud piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attach or fasten one thing to another is a synonym of join.

clue.text: People count on them to send them to sleep

definitions.text: People count on them to send them to sleep

parts.words: People count on them to send them to sleep
parts.note: count on seems to mean rely on, but people literally count farm animals when insomniac

explanation.surface: Relying on something to help one drop off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count on' is literal counting, the old cure for insomnia.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting woolly farm animals jumping a fence is the traditional cure for sleeplessness.

clue.text: Not many vehicles about, but this controls them

definitions.text: Not many vehicles about, but this controls them

parts.words: Not many vehicles about, but this controls them
parts.note: few vehicles is light traffic; turn those two words about to get the road signal that regulates cars

explanation.surface: The roads are quiet, but a signal still governs the cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' swaps the order of the two words meaning 'not many vehicles'.
explanation.definitionFit: A road signal of red, amber and green regulates the flow of cars.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for cut is read from the bottom

parts.note: to cut hair or a hedge is to clip it
solidified means set hard

explanation.surface: Chopped-up frozen fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CLIP into PILC.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily sea fish of the herring family, related to the sardine.

clue.text: Bridge's top man gets a beating

parts.note: a bridge's span is its length across
a king is the top man in a realm

explanation.surface: The leader at the card table suffers a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests the card game, but SPAN is a bridge's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacking given as punishment is a synonym of beating.

clue.text: White pillows can be something hard to get hold of

definitions.text: something hard to get hold of

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of the two words could become something else

explanation.surface: Snowy bedding can be elusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges WHITE PILLOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsh light that recedes when chased, so anything elusive.

clue.text: A metal machine operator in America perhaps

definitions.meaning: a US five-cent coin, which may operate a slot machine

explanation.surface: A metallic mechanic across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: In America this is also the name of the five-cent coin, used to work slot machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery element used in alloys, and the US five-cent coin that works a slot machine.

clue.text: Clergyman taking a point to heart may be fired

indicators.note: taking means the clergyman's title holds the compass point within it

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A vicar who takes a point to heart might lose his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to heart' says N goes into the middle of CANON. 'fired' suggests dismissal but means shot from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A large old artillery piece is something discharged when shot.

clue.text: Inordinately vain man who had a terrible reputation

definitions.text: man who had a terrible reputation

indicators.note: inordinately, meaning excessively, here signals the letters of vain go wild

explanation.surface: An excessively conceited man of dreadful fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inordinately' rearranges VAIN; 'terrible' points to the Russian tsar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsar Ivan IV of Russia was known as 'the Terrible'.

definitions.meaning: the smooth turf around a golf hole where players putt

explanation.surface: Something to apply as a coat of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is golf putting, not putting on.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf area where one putts, and the hue of grass.

indicators.note: holding says the little word in wraps round the abbreviation for company

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated person in a holding company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding company' looks like a business term; 'holding' puts CO inside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person idolised, or a holy image venerated in Orthodox churches.

parts.note: sounds like an iced cascade, but means ice falling as precipitation

explanation.walkthrough: 'waterfall' is read as water falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellets of ice dropping from clouds are frozen precipitation.

clue.text: Father to the French wife of a German husband?

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
au is French for 'to the'

explanation.surface: A priest goes to see a Frenchman's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: AU is French for 'to the'; FRAU is the German word for wife or Mrs.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word used for a married woman or spouse.

clue.text: Is the bounder brought before this court?

definitions.text: Is the bounder brought before this court?

parts.words: Is the bounder brought before this court?
parts.note: a bounder is a cad, but also a jumping marsupial; an irregular mock tribunal is named after the animal

explanation.surface: Will the cad face trial here?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' is an old word for a cad, but here an animal that bounds; an irregular mock trial is a 'kangaroo court'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bounding Australian marsupial lends its name to an unofficial mock tribunal.

indicators.note: fashionable, in its sense of fashioned anew, signals the letters of airman being reshaped

explanation.surface: A designer brand for a stylish pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' rearranges AIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is an Italian fashion house and brand.

parts.note: sounds like a theatre props manager, but means someone who owns rented property

explanation.walkthrough: A theatre's 'property master' handles props; here it is one who owns property.
explanation.definitionFit: The owner who lets out a house or flat is its master.

parts.note: fetching seems to mean attractive, but means retrieving shot game birds for hunters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' means retrieving, and 'game' is shot birds, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever trained to bring back shot birds for hunters.
